claims.text: Acceptance of one allocation criterion is what keeps the three members cooperating.
claims.limit: Synthetic didactic data (Marco, Appendix E); not an observation of any real institution.

system.name: consortium laboratory access
system.scope: weekly allocation of instrument hours among A, B and C

candidate.description: The members' acceptance of one allocation criterion that holds the cooperation together.

capabilities.description: turn requests into a usable weekly schedule

requirements.description: a priority rule every member accepts as fair

vulnerabilities.feasible_path: senior teams bypass the calendar through informal bookings

matrix.scope: allocation inside the consortium for three cycles
matrix.dependency: without accepted criteria every week reopens the dispute
matrix.transmission: each bypass reduces trust and invites defensive over-booking

alternatives: central weekly allocation by the council
substitution.time: one cycle to switch, at a legitimacy cost

matrix.conversion: accepted criteria convert existing hours into predictable access
matrix.revision: if conflicts persist with criteria applied, the dependency is capacity, not cohesion

decisive_point.statement: Council adoption of an appealable priority rule before cycle 1.
decisive_point.enables: members can plan against a known rule

schwerpunkt.focus: Protect the 50 deadline-bound hours every week.
renunciations: no guarantee for deferrable hours in the week requested
minimums: every deferral has a confirmed later slot

own_dependencies: council willingness to enforce the rule on its senior members
